quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main things affect BAC: how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Your sex, physical condition, and whether you have eaten may also affect it.

questions.question: How should you load cargo onto a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items in front of the tank bag. Load should go over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can make it harder to control the motorcycle.

questions.question: When following another vehicle, is it safe to ride on the far side of your lane?

options.text: Yes, because drivers will see you easily.
No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, because a passenger can tell the driver you are there.
No, because the law requires you to ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders to look better.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn your head only, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: In crashes involving both motorcycles and cars, how many are caused by the car driver failing to yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of all crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because the car driver does not properly yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: Do you need hearing protection when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: No, not if you wear a helmet.
Yes, in addition to wearing a helmet.
No, not if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, in addition to wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing even with a helmet. Hearing protection helps prevent damage while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of your lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out from between cars, and cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is how many times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: When making normal stops, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Switch between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping. This should be your habit for all stops, even normal ones.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.

questions.explanation: Good lane positioning helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from blind spots and surface hazards. It also discourages drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through vehicles in front of you.
When the weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions make stopping harder. This includes heavy traffic, poor weather, nighttime riding, when you cannot see ahead, and when visibility is low.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle leans to turn. Press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward to make the motorcycle lean in that direction.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum following distance of two seconds. Increase it to at least three seconds when riding in bad conditions.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down. A tailgater may be focused on you and not notice hazards ahead that require traffic to stop.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind. If a larger animal is chasing you, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: Is riding side-by-side with another rider in a group recommended?

options.text: Yes, to keep the group together.
No, because it blocks escape routes.
No, because it makes motorcycles look like a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because it blocks escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride side-by-side with other riders. Riding in pairs is dangerous because riders block each other's escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Limit how far you ride each day.

questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Do not take artificial stimulants because you may become extremely tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What color are warning signs, and what color are the letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work properly?

options.text: Block all air from passing through.

questions.explanation: A shield must fasten securely, be scratch-free, resist damage, allow side vision, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and fit over glasses if needed.

questions.question: What does proper riding clothing NOT provide?
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you in a crash and protect against weather. They provide comfort, not discomfort.

questions.question: What happens if you brake while turning in a curve?

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more grip on the road.
You may have less grip on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip on the road.
questions.explanation: While turning, your tires are already using grip to make the turn. When you also brake, less grip is left for stopping.

questions.question: As your motorcycle's weight shifts forward while braking, what can you do?

options.text: Reduce pressure on the front brake.

questions.explanation: As your weight moves forward during braking, the front tire has more grip on the road. This means you can apply more front brake pressure.
